कार्यक्रम के विरोध के दौरान छात्रों और कार्यक्रम में शामिल लोगों के बीच मारपीट हुई थी. इसके ठीक एक हफ्ते बाद, 4 अक्टूबर को हिंदू जागरण मंच से जुड़ी रैली कॉलेज के गेट तक पहुंची. छात्रों का आरोप है कि इस दौरान गेट तोड़ने की कोशिश हुई और बाहर से पत्थर और पानी की बोतलें फेंकी गईं. इन घटनाओं के बाद छात्रों ने प्रशासन से सुरक्षा और हमले के आरोपियों के खिलाफ कार्रवाई की मांग की है. छात्रों का कहना है कि जब तक उनकी मांगें पूरी नहीं होतीं, तब तक कॉलेज में पढ़ाई शुरू नहीं की जाएगी. एक हफ्ते में दो घटनाएं गौरतलब है कि 27 सितंबर को कॉलेज प्रशासन ने आरएसएस से जुड़ी संस्था अखिल भारतीय ग्राहक पंचायत (एबीजीपी) को कैंपस में कार्यक्रम आयोजित करने की अनुमति दी थी. स्टूडेंट काउंसिल ने इसका विरोध किया. छात्रों की आपत्ति थी कि कॉलेज के संसाधनों का इस्तेमाल किसी राजनीतिक विचारधारा से जुड़ी संस्था के कार्यक्रम के लिए नहीं किया जाना चाहिए. विरोध के दौरान छात्रों और कार्यक्रम में शामिल लोगों के बीच झड़प हुई. छात्रों का आरोप है कि उनके साथ मारपीट की गई और उन्हें दौड़ाकर पीटा गया. इस घटना में कई छात्र घायल हुए थे. न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री ने इस घटना पर पहले भी रिपोर्ट की है. इस घटना के बाद 4 अक्टूबर को ‘बोंगियो हिंदी जागरण जादवपुर जिला’ नाम के एक फेसबुक पेज पर अजय नगर चौराहे से एसआरएफटीआई तक मार्च निकालने का पोस्टर साझा किया गया. पोस्ट में बंगाली हिंदुओं को जागृत करने की अपील की गई थी. स्टूडेंट काउंसिल के सदस्य नचिकेत के मुताबिक, छात्रों को इस रैली की जानकारी दो दिन पहले ही मिल गई थी. उन्होंने बताया कि छात्रों ने इसकी जानकारी वाइस चांसलर, पुलिस अधिकारियों और सूचना एवं प्रसारण मंत्रालय को दी थी. नचिकेत के मुताबिक, रैली वाले दिन छात्रों ने वीसी से मुलाकात कर सुरक्षा को लेकर चिंता जताई. उनके अनुसार, वीसी ने कहा कि रैली आएगी और इसे रोकना उनके अधिकार क्षेत्र में नहीं है. नचिकेत का यह भी आरोप है कि छात्रों से उनके नाम सामने आने को लेकर धमकी भरे अंदाज में बात की गई. कॉलेज गेट पर पहुंची भीड़ 4 अक्टूबर को निकली रैली में बड़ी संख्या में लोग शामिल हुए. छात्रों के मुताबिक, कई लोगों के हाथों में भगवा झंडे थे और कुछ के पास डंडे भी थे. छात

items.title: South Central 95: Parakala Prabhakar on the ECI, SIR and the deletion of voters
items.summary: In this week’s South Central, hosts Pooja Prasanna and Anisha Sheth are joined by political economist and author Dr Parakala Prabhakar for an extended conversation on the Election Commission of India (ECI), the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the deletion of voters and the larger questions these developments raise about India’s electoral democracy. Pooja begins the conversation by asking Dr Prabhakar about the Indian Express investigation into the Election Commission and the response issued by the poll body. Prabhakar describes the investigation as a significant piece of journalism and argues that the Election Commission’s response did not adequately address several of the specific questions raised by the report, including issues surrounding Form 6 applications, the inclusion of voters and the deletion of names from electoral rolls. He also points to objections and notes reportedly raised by the other two Election Commissioners, questioning why these concerns were not addressed. The conversation then turns to the functioning of the three-member Election Commission and the role of the Chief Election Commissioner. Dr Prabhakar says that the three Election Commissioners have equal status and that the Chief Election Commissioner is “first among equals”, rather than being the supreme authority within the Commission. The discussion then moves to the Election Commission’s claim that the Special Intensive Revision has been endorsed by the Supreme Court. Prabhakar questions the extent of that endorsement, particularly in relation to changes made to Form 6 after the court’s decision. He also asks whether the scale of deletions is consistent with India’s growing population and argues that the process deserves greater scrutiny. The conversation then looks at what the deletions could mean for the legitimacy of elections themselves. If the Election Commission now considers large numbers of people who appeared on earlier electoral rolls to have been ineligible, Dr Prabhakar asks what that means for elections that were conducted using those same rolls. Prabhakar argues that this raises questions about the credibility of previous elections as well as future ones. “If they say that they are cleaning up the electoral roll, it is assumed that the previous electoral rolls were not clean,” he says, questioning the implications of that position for elections conducted using those rolls. items.title: Who altered Form 6: Did the Supreme Court just torpedo ECI’s ‘court approval’ defence?
items.summary: With each passing day, the Election Commission has more to explain about the conduct of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. On Monday, the Supreme Court questioned one of the Commission’s most consequential claims on the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR): that the modified Form 6 declaration had the court’s approval. The clarification from Chief Justice Surya Kant matters because the Commission did not merely refer to the Supreme Court judgment as background. In its September 26 statement , the ECI had suggested that the new declaration attached to Form 6 was consistent with, and approved by, the Supreme Court’s May 2026 judgment on Bihar SIR. The court has now made it clear that it did not approve any modified Form 6. #BREAKING "Modified Form 6 has not been approved by us, let us be very clear" - CJI Surya Kant. #ElectionCommisisonofIndia — Live Law (@LiveLawIndia) October 5, 2026 Consider the chronology. The modified declaration was introduced after the Supreme Court’s May judgment. The new version requires a person applying for inclusion to state whether they or their parents were included or mapped in the previous SIR. However, five days ago this modification was taken back by ECI. This was not part of the earlier Form 6 used in the SIR exercise. The very legality of this change had already become a point of disagreement within the Commission, with Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objecting that the statutory Form 6 could not be changed without an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. And yet, despite those objections, the modified form was introduced. When the internal disagreement was reported, the Commission’s September 26 statement offered a defence by referring to the Supreme Court’s Bihar SIR judgment. But Monday’s hearing has now complicated that explanation considerably. The CJI went a step further, saying that once the records are produced, the court would want to know who modified the form. Despite criticism from the Opposition , the Commission has not backed down. In a 'fact check' posted on X on October 5, it said the Bihar SIR order was issued “with the unanimous approval of the Commission” and upheld by the Supreme Court on May 27, 2026. It also cited its Press Note No. 120, which states that “the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court.” That is a claim about a declaration the Commission itself withdrew days ago. items.title: Can DRTs accept written statements after 45 days? Delhi, Telangana and P&H High Courts differ
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that Debts Recovery Tribunals (DRTs) cannot accept written statements beyond 45 days under the Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act [Nikhil Podar Vs PNB]. However, the Telangana High Court and the Punjab and Haryana High Court have taken the opposite view. A Division Bench of Justices Subramonium Prasad and Renu Bhatnagar of Delhi High Court held that the 30-day period prescribed for filing a written statement can be extended by a maximum of 15 days, and that courts have no power to condone any further delay. “ The delay beyond the maximum period 45 days prescribed under Section 19(5)(i) of the RDB Act cannot be condoned by any Court," the Court said. Justice Subramonium Prasad The Court was hearing a petition filed by Nikhil Poddar against a Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal (DRAT) order refusing to take his written statement on record in recovery proceedings initiated by Punjab National Bank. Poddar's counsel received the complete pleadings/ paper book on September 6, 2019. The written statement was filed on November 26, beyond the 45-day period. The High Court rejected his argument concerning delay by the bank in supplying the papers, finding that the entire paper book had been received on September 6 and that limitation began running from that date. The Bench said the RDB Act is a special code and held that Section 5 of the Limitation Act could not be invoked to condone the delay. It also relied on Supreme Court decisions concerning statutory timelines under the Consumer Protection Act, Arbitration and Conciliation Act, Central Excise Act and Companies Act. The ruling follows the Delhi High Court's 2021 decision in Anita Garg v. State Bank of India , which held that the words “not exceeding fifteen days” restrict the DRT's discretion to extend time beyond the additional 15-day period. The Punjab and Haryana High Court, however, took a different view in March 2026. In Shri Shri Ram Gupta v. Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal , Chief Justice Sheel Nagu and Justice Sanjiv Berry held that the provisions governing filing of written statements under the RDB Act, read with Order VIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, are directory and not mandatory. Consequently, it set aside orders refusing written statements and gave the petitioners a final opportunity to file them. The Telangana High Court also recognised a DRT's power to go beyond 45 days. items.title: Don't allow circumstances, doubts to limit achievements: Justice Sunita Agarwal to women lawyers
items.summary: Gujarat High Court Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal on Monday urged young women lawyers not to allow circumstances, expectations or others’ doubts to limit their achievements. Addressing her farewell reference at the High Court, Justice Agarwal recalled that she had faced similar obstacles during her career. “Do not allow circumstances, expectations and doubts of others to determine the limits of your achievements. In my career I have met the same obstacles as you and it was perseverance which carried me through,” said Justice Agarwal. She called upon women already established at the bar and the bench to guide and encourage younger lawyers. “To the women already established in the profession on the bench or at the bar whichever rung of the professional ladder you stand on today, hold the hands of those who are climbing up guide them, nurture them and give them the confidence to persevere,” added Justice Agarwal. Justice Agarwal also offered advice to young members of the Bar, urging them to read extensively, prepare thoroughly and remain humble. “My advice to you is this, grab whatever opportunity comes your way, read a lot, prepare well as if each case were your first and remain attentive and humble throughout your arguments,” she said. Justice Agarwal added, “Success at the bar may come in different forms and at different stages but the reputation you build through integrity, hard work and humility will remain your most lasting asset.” Justice Agarwal recalled beginning her legal career at the Allahabad High Court at a time when work was scarce and she was uncertain about where her career would lead. "Whatever I am today and whatever I have achieved I owe to the institution that embraced, nurtured and protected me," she said. Reflecting on her tenure, Justice Agarwal described the past three years as a turning point in her professional and personal growth and among the most challenging years of her life. "These years taught me to keep going despite the difficulties around me, to stay grounded and to keep working without losing my grit," she said. Justice Agarwal also highlighted the High Court's efforts towards automation and digitalisation, including the launch of a pilot for a paperless court. “Whatever changes we have brought about through our collective efforts all have been directed towards strengthening the institution by institutionalizing every function rather than personalizing it,” noted Justice Agarwal. items.title: It is a complete Catch-22 situation for voters: Bombay High Court questions rejection of Form 8 during SIR
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Monday flagged the "complete Catch-22 situation" being faced by voters who have changed their residences in the recent past [Paresh Salgaonkar v. State of Goa & Ors.] A division bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar noted that current guidelines leave electors, who have shifted residences, without a legitimate remedy during the revision process. It noted that the relocated electors are forced to submit Form 6 for new enrolment when their Form 8 for address modification is getting rejected. Form 6 requires voters to declare that they are not registered elsewhere. “The Form 6, it is a false declaration. He gives you Form 8, you say I cannot touch your Form 8, you must give the enumeration. He says, I do not want to give the enumeration, I am giving you Form 8. But section 21 says you have to hear him before removing his name, not from the draft, from the original role,” the Court said. Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. Jamsandekar The High Court probed the core purpose of conducting a Special Intensive Revision. While questioning the rationale behind dropping voters during the revision process, the Court observed: "Entire SIR procedure was on the basis that had to find out whether an elector is actually an Indian citizen or not. The basis of the SIR was not to see whether the voter is there or not. It is to find out whether he is an Indian citizen or not," the court said. Advocate Gauresh Agni, appearing for the ECI, submitted " There were illegal immigrants also." The Bench addressed this submission by countering: "So, will this subserve the purpose by a Form 6 or a Form 8? Judgment [of the Supreme Court on Bihar SIR nowhere says that the manner of doing this is going to be by Form 6. Law is either by the legislature or if it is delegated, or a rule-making power." The Court further questioned the ECI on its broader constitutional duties. “If, by this process, citizens are excluded, then how do we read this mandate?” The Bench asserted that the ECI’s primary constitutional obligation remains the prevention of disenfranchisement of eligible citizens. The Court was hearing a batch of petitions challenging the Election Commission of India (ECI)'s automated rejection of Form 8 applications submitted for updating voter addresses in Goa. items.title: Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre appointed Acting Chief Justice of Delhi High Court
items.summary: Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre was appointed as the Acting Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court on Monday. The Union Ministry of Law and Justice issued a notification in this regard after Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya was elevated to the Supreme Court . "In exercise of the power conferred by Article 223 of the Constitution of India, the President is pleased to appoint Shri Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre, Judge of the Delhi High Court, to perform the duties of office of the Chief Justice of that High Court with effect from the date Shri Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya relinquishes the charge of the office of Chief Justice consequent upon his elevation as a Judge of the Supreme Court of India,” the ministry said in a notification. Justice Sambre was born on December 19, 1967 at Nagpur. He graduated in law in 1992 from University College of Law, Nagpur. He enrolled as an advocate on August 25, 1992 and started legal career with then Senior Advocate Sharad A Bobde (former Chief Justice of India). Justice Sambre practised before the High Court of Bombay, Nagpur and was the Secretary of the High Court Bar Association, Nagpur for 2004-07. He was elevated as a judge of Bombay High Court on January 6, 2014. He was transferred to the Delhi High Court in July 2025.

items.title: Centre appoints Gurvinder Pal Singh as additional judge of Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Central government on Monday notified the appointment of judicial officer Gurvinder Pal Singh as an additional judge of the Delhi High Court. The notification was issued by Union Law and Justice Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal. The appointment comes nearly a month after the Supreme Court Collegium had recommended Singh's appointment along with seven other judicial officers on September 10. The Collegium had recommended eight names for appointment as judges of the Delhi High Court. Singh was the only one among the eight whose appointment had not been notified in the Centre's earlier notification dated September 19. items.title: Low IQ or intellectual disability alone won't make an accused unfit to stand trial: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently held that low intelligence quotient (IQ) or an intellectual disability alone is not enough to declare that an accused is incapable of defending themselves before a court or unfit to stand trial. [Kamal Raj v State of Kerala] Justice Jobin Sebastian explained that Section 368 the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) lays down the procedure to be followed in case a person of unsound mind is tried before court. Under this provision, courts are required to enquire into the accused person's mental condition, their capacity to defend themselves and to postpone criminal proceedings if they are found incapable of making their defence. The Court stated that the important issue to be considered is whether the mental condition or disability prevents the accused from understanding the nature of the proceedings, whether they can understand the questions put to them and communicate the necessary facts and instructions to their lawyer. " The mere presence of an intellectual disability or a low IQ, by itself, will not make a person incapacitated to stand trial, " the Court said. Justice Jobin Sebastian The September 29 ruling came on a petition filed by a 20-year-old accused in a case a pending before a Punalur special court under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. Raj claimed that he had an intellectual disability which made him incapable of defending himself and sought postponement of trial under Section 368 of the BNSS. The trial court conducted an inquiry into his claim and found that he was fit to stand trial. Raj then approached the High Court challenging the trial court's finding. His counsel argued that the trial court had not properly considered the medical evidence. In particular, he pointed to a medical board report which recorded Raj's IQ as 35 and another medical assessment which stated that his social age was only 10 years. It was also pointed out that Raj had faced development difficulty since childhood and had required assistance throughout his schooling, including the use of a scribe during examinations. However, the medical moard which examined Raj had found that despite his intellectual disability, he could understand the allegations made against him and the nature of the court proceedings as well as comprehend and respond to the questions posed to him. items.title: NUSRL Ranchi students hold protest over women's safety and hostel restrictions
items.summary: Students of National University of Study and Research in Law (NUSRL), Ranchi protested on October 3 over women's safety and hostel rules. The protest ran from about 2 AM to 7 AM, with a few faculty members attending. According to sources, it has ended and the issues are being resolved internally. An email sent to the Vice-Chancellor's (VC) office, the Registrar and the Dean listed 14 concerns from the girls' hostel. Students alleged that labourers frequently move through student areas, some inadequately clothed. They claimed workers have begun living in the new library building near residences. They also said that male workers enter the girls' hostel without adequate notice and that the warning bell is hard to hear. They have sought a fixed, notified schedule. Female students have alleged that some recently posted guards stare at them intrusively and have sought sensitisation, supervision and accountability for security staff. Students also said that several areas on campus and outside the gate are poorly lit and lack CCTV cameras. They alleged that female students have faced eve-teasing shortly after leaving the campus. They also also pointed out that they must seek permission and send emails before leaving the hostel and that calls are made to check whether they reached home. They allege that the boys' hostel has no such system, suggesting gender discrimination. The email, sent on October 3, also said that the administration had not offered direct dialogue. They questioned if they could even raise campus issues without facing disciplinary action and sought a transparent process for sexual harassment complaints. They also flagged a broken sanitary machine. A student also linked the protest to an allegation that the administration was shielding another student over a social media post that many found objectionable. Bar & Bench attempted to reach the NUSRL administration for comment, to no avail.

items.title: India’s women are angry, rightfully so | Let Me Explain 168 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: India’s women are angry. Those are slogans from thousands of women and students who have taken to the streets in Delhi over the past week, demanding something that should really not have to be a demand: the right to study, work, travel, and simply exist in public without being afraid of sexual violence. The immediate trigger was the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in south Delhi. The response was swift, but not in the way the protesters wanted. Lady Shri Ram College, a women’s college close to the park, was forced to switch to online classes. Delhi authorities wanted to restrict access to public parks after dark, and announced security measures for vulnerable areas- which they should have done much before. And for many women, that is precisely the problem. Because this isn't really about one case, or even one city. It is about a pattern that has become painfully familiar. A woman is assaulted, there is outrage. And sooner or later comes the advice: don’t go there, don’t stay out late, dress differently, carry something for protection, call someone when you reach home. In other words, the crime happens to a woman, and somehow it’s still the woman who gets saddled with a new set of rules. And this policing of women very easily escalates to harassment as well In Jamui of Bihar, two teenagers were physically harassed by a group of men claiming to be enforcing “morality”. A video of the incident also went viral, eventually leading to police action. So why does every conversation about women’s safety seem to come with another rule for women? Why does an unsafe public space become a reason to restrict the women who use it? And why, exactly, are women so angry? Let me explain. And before we get into it, a quick word about why we’re able to have conversations like this. At The News Minute, the topic of gender isn’t something we dust off when there’s a rape case in the headlines. It is a part of our journalism every day. We report on sexual violence, but we also ask what comes before it, what happens after it, and how institutions respond And we are entirely supported by VIEWERS like you. items.title: Rift in Congress: UDF convener complains to high command against CM Satheesan
items.summary: Senior Congress leader and United Democratic Front (UDF) convener Adoor Prakash has reportedly filed a formal complaint against Kerala Chief Minister VD Satheesan with the All India Congress Committee (AICC) high command on Monday, October 5. The complaint was submitted directly to Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge in New Delhi, and the complaint demanded the high command’s urgent intervention against Satheesan taking decisions unilaterally. Earlier, on October 1, in a press conference, Adoor Prakash, who also serves as a Member of Parliament (MP) in the Lok Sabha representing the Attingal constituency, accused Satheesan of taking major government and policy decisions unilaterally without proper consultation with the party leadership or alliance partners. He alleged that he has been deliberately kept in the dark and frequently learns about significant administration and alliance decisions only through social media and news outlets. The conflict between the UDF convener and CM VD Satheesan has come to the fore just four months after the UDF came to power in Kerala. Congress President Shri @kharge met Shri @AdoorPrakash. New Delhi https://t.co/vtZjAjgO2x — Congress (@INCIndia) October 5, 2026 On October 5, after meeting Kharge, Adoor Prakash didn’t respond to media queries; however, he said “yes” when a reporter asked whether he had met Kharge and communicated the issues. The rift stemmed from the government's decision to appoint IUML leader MK Muneer as chairman of the State Administrative Reforms Commission and Forward Bloc leader G Devarajan as the State government’s representative in New Delhi. These two positions carry Cabinet rank. Adoor Prakash told the media that he was not informed about these decisions. “Both of them are deserving people. I am not saying that they are not eligible. But, as the UDF convenor, I was not informed in any way about such matters, nor was there any discussion or communication that we were going to take such a decision,” Adoor Prakash said.

items.title: ‘Repeatedly erased’: Trans filmmaker flags misgendering, non-inclusivity at IDSFFK
items.summary: When trans non-binary filmmaker Harshappi Harsh (they/them) arrived at the 18th International Documentary and Short Film Festival of Kerala (IDSFFK) as a guest filmmaker, they expected to screen their film, meet fellow filmmakers, and spend time with friends. Instead, they said they spent much of the festival correcting people who repeatedly misgendered them, looking for a toilet they could comfortably use, and raising concerns about a lack of inclusivity at the festival. Harshappi, a transmasculine non-binary photographer, filmmaker, and community organiser from Thiruvananthapuram, had their 20-minute documentary To Stitch Together a Watermelon Heart selected for the short documentary competition at the festival. The film, which is based on Harshappi’s own experiences, explores their journey as a trans non-binary person and questions the erasure of trans and queer experiences. But Harshappi’s own experience at the festival left them feeling repeatedly erased. “I came here with my film to enjoy some time with my friends and showcase my work. I did not come here to advocate for basic rights,” Harshappi told TNM. According to Harshappi, the problems began from the day they arrived. Despite informing the organisers that they were a transmasculine non-binary person, they were repeatedly misgendered by festival officials and others. They said they corrected people several times. “This is something very basic. They could have just called me by my name,” Harshappi said. The repeated misgendering was not limited to informal interactions, the filmmaker said. Their name and gender were also allegedly incorrectly represented during official festival proceedings. The official IDSFFK website describes Harshappi as a trans non-binary person. In a promotional video released on September 29 about their film, Harshappi said they were identified correctly as a transmasculine person. But when they checked the video the following morning, they found that they had been misgendered in the caption and that the video’s title feminised their identity. Their friends had to repeatedly comment on the festival's social media post before the organisers corrected it, Harshappi said, adding that the festival team did not apologise to them for the error. items.title: ‘Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us’: CJI Surya Kant
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday, October 5 clarified that it had not approved the modified Form 6 being used by the Election Commission of India (ECI) during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the observation while hearing a petition challenging alleged unilateral decisions taken by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. “Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let’s be clear. When the record is produced, we would like to see who has modified,” CJI Surya Kant observed . The clarification comes after the ECI said in a press note on September 26 that the declaration attached to Form 6 for the SIR exercise had been approved by the Supreme Court. “The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as Rules (Registration of Electors Roles 1960) will be used,” the ECI had said . The controversy relates to changes made to Form 6, which is used by people seeking inclusion in electoral rolls. The online Form 6 application was altered in July, during the third phase of the SIR, to require applicants to provide their parents’ details from the previous SIR. The change was made after the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgement concerning the SIR in Bihar. The ECI’s claim that the Supreme Court had upheld the additional declaration had come under scrutiny because of what the May judgement actually said about the poll panel’s powers. The SC had held that the ECI retained a degree of authority to formulate an appropriate documentation framework for an SIR. However, the court also said that this authority was “not unbounded” and had to remain within the existing statutory scheme. The judgement said, “In devising such a framework, the Commission must remain cognisant of the existing statutory scheme, and any departure therefrom must be informed by a rational nexus to the object sought to be achieved.” It further said: “The formulation of the documentation regime must thus reflect a calibrated balance in drawing from the statutory framework, while adapting it, where necessary, to effectively serve the purpose of ensuring the accuracy and integrity of the electoral roll.” The Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, flowing from Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, prescribe the framework for electoral forms. items.title: Telangana SIR: Congress seeks SIT probe into alleged Form-7 misuse
items.summary: The Telangana Congress has sought the formation of a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the alleged misuse of Form 7s under the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR). The party alleged that pre-filled Form-7 applications are being prepared and submitted in multiple constituencies in Hyderabad in an attempt to delete the names of Congress leaders, workers, their family members, and other genuine voters from electoral rolls. The demand for the SIT was made in a letter, dated October 5, to the Hyderabad City Commissioner of Police by Pulipati Rajesh Kumar, Election Commission Coordination Committee chairman of the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee. “Any organised attempt to misuse Form-7 applications to remove genuine voters through false declarations, fabricated particulars or impersonation must be treated with the utmost seriousness,” the letter said. Similar reports from three constituencies According to the complaint, incidents of Form-7 misuse were reported in Musheerabad, Bahadurpura, and Goshamahal constituencies in Hyderabad. The similar nature of the reports across three constituencies raises suspicions of a “larger coordinated operation,” it alleged. Regarding Musheerabad, the complaint alleges that BJP Booth Level Agent (BLA) Sivegi Balachander alias Balu submitted Form-7 applications seeking deletion of the name of Congress BLA Sharafuddin and around 31 members of his family. The Congress has questioned whether those named in the applications had actually submitted or authorised them. TNM had previously reported about the alleged Form-7 misuse by BLA Balachander in Musheerabad. Hyderabad Muslim voters say BJP BLA sought their deletion despite knowing them since childhood In Bahadurpura, similar pre-printed Form-7 applications were reportedly detected on October 1, according to the complaint. In Goshamahal, around 15 pre-printed Form-7 applications were allegedly brought by a BJP BLA for submission to the Booth Level Officer (BLO) at polling booth 173 on October 3. The BLO reportedly did not accept them as they did not carry the signatures of the respective applicants and were submitted in bulk, the complaint said. Rajesh Kumar has sought an investigation into whether the applications originated from a common source or database and whether electoral details of Congress leaders, workers, their families and other voters were collected and used without their knowledge or consent. items.title: Kumbh fame Monalisa Bhosle gets relief as MP HC sets aside birth record change
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court has set aside an order cancelling the birth certificate of Monalisa Bhosle, the young woman who became an internet sensation after videos of her selling rudraksha beads at the 2025 Prayag Maha Kumbh went viral. The Indore Bench of the High Court, in an order passed on Wednesday, October 1, held that Monalisa was not given an opportunity to be heard before her birth record was changed. It directed the Chief Municipal Officer (CMO) of Maheshwar in Khargone district to reconsider the matter after giving her an effective opportunity to present her case. The court, however, did not determine whether Monalisa was born in 2008 or 2009, which is at the heart of the legal dispute surrounding her marriage to actor Farman Khan. Instead, it set aside the cancellation order on the ground that it was passed without hearing the person directly affected by it. “It is, thus, trite that any action prejudicial to a citizen, which is taken by the State or public authority without affording him an opportunity of being heard, would be unfair and arbitrary,” Justice Gajendra Singh said. The ruling comes months after Monalisa’s March 2026 marriage to Farman, a Muslim man from Uttar Pradesh, became the centre of a political and legal controversy involving allegations of “love jihad”, questions over her age, and an abduction case against her husband. It also comes after a National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) inquiry concluded that Monalisa was a minor at the time of the marriage, based on a hospital record from Madhya Pradesh that recorded her date of birth as December 30, 2009. Monalisa and Farman have disputed this, maintaining that she was born on January 1, 2008, as reflected in several government-issued documents. TNM has previously reported in detail on the competing claims over Monalisa’s age, the birth records involving her and her family, and how her marriage became a political and legal flashpoint between Kerala and Madhya Pradesh.
